Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

### Key decisions
- **Pin bump only — no gate migration.** 0.10.0's `duplication` gate is per-FILE (max measured 60.65%, 246 files >1%), while the repo's enforced guards are global-% jscpd ratchets (lib <1%, app <3.7%, cross-module <0.31%). Swapping would change enforcement semantics; the native `duplication.sources` key is documented in `crap4dart.yaml` as available if the jscpd guards are ever retired.
- **Static + empirical drift proof:** the 0.10.0 analysis pipeline (`complexity.dart`, `crap_score.dart`, `crap_analyzer.dart`, `dart_parser.dart`, `config.dart`) is byte-identical to 0.9.5; only `method_extractor.dart` migrated to the analyzer-14 AST (naming/`isComplete`, score-neutral). Verified: 6466 core + 5407 app methods — zero set or complexity diffs between versions.
- Updated the stale tool pin in AGENTS.md (said `0.2.1`) and annotated the three CI activation sites.

### How to verify
```bash
dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
dart pub global run crap4dart analyze   # Max CRAP 12.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)
dart pub global run crap4dart check     # 2 gates passed, 0 warned
python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down <base>   # badge/parity/only-down OK
```
Local CI-parity run (ambient `FA_*` stripped): 7898 tests passed; coverage 93.49% ≥ 80%; 0.9.5 and 0.10.0 report the identical max CRAP (12.0) on the same lcov.

### Notes for the next lane
- **Pre-existing, not from this change:** `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` (3 tests: `move reorders and persists`, `remove 0 persists…`, `add appends…`) reads the REAL `Platform.environment` via `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` (no `env:` seam) — running the suite from inside a fa session (which sets `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) flips those edits onto the env-refusal arm and fails them. CI is unaffected; fixing needs a small env seam in `AgentCliConfig`.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. ## PR Description

### What changed
Bumped the crap4dart CI pin `>=0.9.5` → `>=0.10.0` (gh-1061: upstream shipped `duplication.sources` — the cross-module scan no longer needs the `--config` temp-config variant) and verified the 0.10.0 analyzer-14.4 refresh against the full CI-parity pipeline.

### Key decisions
- **Pin bump only — no gate migration.** 0.10.0's `duplication` gate is per-FILE (max measured 60.65%, 246 files >1%), while the repo's enforced guards are global-% jscpd ratchets (lib <1%, app <3.7%, cross-module <0.31%). Swapping would change enforcement semantics; the native `duplication.sources` key is documented in `crap4dart.yaml` as available if the jscpd guards are ever retired.
- **Static + empirical drift proof:** the 0.10.0 analysis pipeline (`complexity.dart`, `crap_score.dart`, `crap_analyzer.dart`, `dart_parser.dart`, `config.dart`) is byte-identical to 0.9.5; only `method_extractor.dart` migrated to the analyzer-14 AST (naming/`isComplete`, score-neutral). Verified: 6466 core + 5407 app methods — zero set or complexity diffs between versions.
- Updated the stale tool pin in AGENTS.md (said `0.2.1`) and annotated the three CI activation sites.

### How to verify
```bash
dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
dart pub global run crap4dart analyze   # Max CRAP 12.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)
dart pub global run crap4dart check     # 2 gates passed, 0 warned
python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down <base>   # badge/parity/only-down OK
```
Local CI-parity run (ambient `FA_*` stripped): 7898 tests passed; coverage 93.49% ≥ 80%; 0.9.5 and 0.10.0 report the identical max CRAP (12.0) on the same lcov.

### Notes for the next lane
- **Pre-existing, not from this change:** `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` (3 tests: `move reorders and persists`, `remove 0 persists…`, `add appends…`) reads the REAL `Platform.environment` via `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` (no `env:` seam) — running the suite from inside a fa session (which sets `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) flips those edits onto the env-refusal arm and fails them. CI is unaffected; fixing needs a small env seam in `AgentCliConfig`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).

blocks.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. - **Updated**: 2026-09-28T21:19:28Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Bumped the crap4dart CI pin `>=0.9.5` → `>=0.10.0` (gh-1061: upstream shipped `duplication.sources` — the cross-module scan no longer needs the `--config` temp-config variant) and verified the 0.10.0 analyzer-14.4 refresh against the full CI-parity pipeline.

### Key decisions
- **Pin bump only — no gate migration.** 0.10.0's `duplication` gate is per-FILE (max measured 60.65%, 246 files >1%), while the repo's enforced guards are global-% jscpd ratchets (lib <1%, app <3.7%, cross-module <0.31%). Swapping would change enforcement semantics; the native `duplication.sources` key is documented in `crap4dart.yaml` as available if the jscpd guards are ever retired.
- **Static + empirical drift proof:** the 0.10.0 analysis pipeline (`complexity.dart`, `crap_score.dart`, `crap_analyzer.dart`, `dart_parser.dart`, `config.dart`) is byte-identical to 0.9.5; only `method_extractor.dart` migrated to the analyzer-14 AST (naming/`isComplete`, score-neutral). Verified: 6466 core + 5407 app methods — zero set or complexity diffs between versions.
- Updated the stale tool pin in AGENTS.md (said `0.2.1`) and annotated the three CI activation sites.

### How to verify
```bash
dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
dart pub global run crap4dart analyze   # Max CRAP 12.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)
dart pub global run crap4dart check     # 2 gates passed, 0 warned
python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down <base>   # badge/parity/only-down OK
```
Local CI-parity run (ambient `FA_*` stripped): 7898 tests passed; coverage 93.49% ≥ 80%; 0.9.5 and 0.10.0 report the identical max CRAP (12.0) on the same lcov.

### Notes for the next lane
- **Pre-existing, not from this change:** `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` (3 tests: `move reorders and persists`, `remove 0 persists…`, `add appends…`) reads the REAL `Platform.environment` via `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` (no `env:` seam) — running the suite from inside a fa session (which sets `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) flips those edits onto the env-refusal arm and fails them. CI is unaffected; fixing needs a small env seam in `AgentCliConfig`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;
  child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly (issue #553).
  Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps the full
  real-provider suite (pty-integration).
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green
  (includes golden suite; integration-tagged `test/cli_visual` runs in the
  nightly workflow + on demand).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80% (full ratchet on main/nightly; PRs ratchet
  CHANGED lines via `scripts/diff_coverage.py`); jscpd duplication < 1%
  core `lib/`, < 3.7% `flutter_app/lib/` (ratchet — only tighten).
- Cross-module duplication (issue #487): clones spanning module roots
  (`lib`, `bin`, `flutter_app/lib`, `packages/*/lib`, `browser_ext/dart`)
  via `scripts/check_dup_cross_module.sh` — stage `dupx`, ONE jscpd

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — the gate's per-file semantics and the
  # 0.10.0 `duplication.sources` cross-module key stay available if the
  # jscpd guards are ever retired
  duplication: {enabled: false}
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. - **Updated**: 2026-09-28T21:19:28Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Bumped the crap4dart CI pin `>=0.9.5` → `>=0.10.0` (gh-1061: upstream shipped `duplication.sources` — the cross-module scan no longer needs the `--config` temp-config variant) and verified the 0.10.0 analyzer-14.4 refresh against the full CI-parity pipeline.

### Key decisions
- **Pin bump only — no gate migration.** 0.10.0's `duplication` gate is per-FILE (max measured 60.65%, 246 files >1%), while the repo's enforced guards are global-% jscpd ratchets (lib <1%, app <3.7%, cross-module <0.31%). Swapping would change enforcement semantics; the native `duplication.sources` key is documented in `crap4dart.yaml` as available if the jscpd guards are ever retired.
- **Static + empirical drift proof:** the 0.10.0 analysis pipeline (`complexity.dart`, `crap_score.dart`, `crap_analyzer.dart`, `dart_parser.dart`, `config.dart`) is byte-identical to 0.9.5; only `method_extractor.dart` migrated to the analyzer-14 AST (naming/`isComplete`, score-neutral). Verified: 6466 core + 5407 app methods — zero set or complexity diffs between versions.
- Updated the stale tool pin in AGENTS.md (said `0.2.1`) and annotated the three CI activation sites.

### How to verify
```bash
dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
dart pub global run crap4dart analyze   # Max CRAP 12.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)
dart pub global run crap4dart check     # 2 gates passed, 0 warned
python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down <base>   # badge/parity/only-down OK
```
Local CI-parity run (ambient `FA_*` stripped): 7898 tests passed; coverage 93.49% ≥ 80%; 0.9.5 and 0.10.0 report the identical max CRAP (12.0) on the same lcov.

### Notes for the next lane
- **Pre-existing, not from this change:** `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` (3 tests: `move reorders and persists`, `remove 0 persists…`, `add appends…`) reads the REAL `Platform.environment` via `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` (no `env:` seam) — running the suite from inside a fa session (which sets `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) flips those edits onto the env-refusal arm and fails them. CI is unaffected; fixing needs a small env seam in `AgentCliConfig`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.

  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; real-provider files carry `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and
  run ONLY in the tag-only provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets;

blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — the gate's per-file semantics and the
  # 0.10.0 `duplication.sources` cross-module key stay available if the
  # jscpd guards are ever retired
  duplication: {enabled: false}
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan; the
          # duplication gate stays jscpd-gated, see crap4dart.yaml).
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Broken-goldens gate over core test/ goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:

        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

## PR Description

### What changed
Bumped the crap4dart CI pin `>=0.9.5` → `>=0.10.0` (gh-1061: upstream shipped `duplication.sources` — the cross-module scan no longer needs the `--config` temp-config variant) and verified the 0.10.0 analyzer-14.4 refresh against the full CI-parity pipeline.

### Key decisions
- **Pin bump only — no gate migration.** 0.10.0's `duplication` gate is per-FILE (max measured 60.65%, 246 files >1%), while the repo's enforced guards are global-% jscpd ratchets (lib <1%, app <3.7%, cross-module <0.31%). Swapping would change enforcement semantics; the native `duplication.sources` key is documented in `crap4dart.yaml` as available if the jscpd guards are ever retired.
- **Static + empirical drift proof:** the 0.10.0 analysis pipeline (`complexity.dart`, `crap_score.dart`, `crap_analyzer.dart`, `dart_parser.dart`, `config.dart`) is byte-identical to 0.9.5; only `method_extractor.dart` migrated to the analyzer-14 AST (naming/`isComplete`, score-neutral). Verified: 6466 core + 5407 app methods — zero set or complexity diffs between versions.
- Updated the stale tool pin in AGENTS.md (said `0.2.1`) and annotated the three CI activation sites.

### How to verify
```bash
dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
dart pub global run crap4dart analyze   # Max CRAP 12.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)
dart pub global run crap4dart check     # 2 gates passed, 0 warned
python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down <base>   # badge/parity/only-down OK
```
Local CI-parity run (ambient `FA_*` stripped): 7898 tests passed; coverage 93.49% ≥ 80%; 0.9.5 and 0.10.0 report the identical max CRAP (12.0) on the same lcov.

### Notes for the next lane
- **Pre-existing, not from this change:** `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` (3 tests: `move reorders and persists`, `remove 0 persists…`, `add appends…`) reads the REAL `Platform.environment` via `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` (no `env:` seam) — running the suite from inside a fa session (which sets `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) flips those edits onto the env-refusal arm and fails them. CI is unaffected; fixing needs a small env seam in `AgentCliConfig`.

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — the gate's per-file semantics and the
  # 0.10.0 `duplication.sources` cross-module key stay available if the
  # jscpd guards are ever retired
  duplication: {enabled: false}
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - name: Pub cache (crap4dart)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}
          restore-keys: pub-crap4dart-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: app-coverage-shard-*
          path: app-coverage-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          count=$(ls app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "2" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 2 app shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p flutter_app/coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info \
            app-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: Config guards — badge sync, exclude parity, only-down (AC1/E1/AC3)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          [ -n "$BASE_SHA" ] || BASE_SHA=HEAD~1
          python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: pin bumped 0.2.1 → >=0.9.5 for the gate framework.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 (analyzer 14.4 refresh).
          # coverage.run_tests: false in both configs — the merged shard
          # lcov above is the source; never re-run the suite here.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
          cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze --format json > crap_report.json

      # Issue #490 AC2: publish the ranked CRAP JSON even when the ratchet
      # is red (analyze writes the report to stdout before its non-zero
      # exit) — descents rank from this artifact, never from a local
      # ad-hoc run.
      - name: Upload crap_report.json artifact (issue 490 AC2)
        if: always() && (needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: crap_report
          path: flutter_app/crap_report.json
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Pixel and flutter gates over test/golden/goldens (issue 447)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart check

  # Issue #283: fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by the test-core template — a
  # duration-balanced manifest (scripts/faui_test_shards.json, rebalanced
  # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml), one file executed by exactly ONE shard,
  # goldens excluded exactly as before (host-locked). Shards fan out INSIDE
  # the job graph; only the aggregate Quality gate is a required check, so
  # a red shard = red gate and path-skipped = neutral (AC4 semantics). A
  # single failed matrix leg can be rerun alone via "Re-run failed jobs"
  # (E1) — the gate then re-aggregates the same results.
  test-faui:
    name: fa_ui tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 12
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:

instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. ## PR Description

### What changed
Bumped the crap4dart CI pin `>=0.9.5` → `>=0.10.0` (gh-1061: upstream shipped `duplication.sources` — the cross-module scan no longer needs the `--config` temp-config variant) and verified the 0.10.0 analyzer-14.4 refresh against the full CI-parity pipeline.

### Key decisions
- **Pin bump only — no gate migration.** 0.10.0's `duplication` gate is per-FILE (max measured 60.65%, 246 files >1%), while the repo's enforced guards are global-% jscpd ratchets (lib <1%, app <3.7%, cross-module <0.31%). Swapping would change enforcement semantics; the native `duplication.sources` key is documented in `crap4dart.yaml` as available if the jscpd guards are ever retired.
- **Static + empirical drift proof:** the 0.10.0 analysis pipeline (`complexity.dart`, `crap_score.dart`, `crap_analyzer.dart`, `dart_parser.dart`, `config.dart`) is byte-identical to 0.9.5; only `method_extractor.dart` migrated to the analyzer-14 AST (naming/`isComplete`, score-neutral). Verified: 6466 core + 5407 app methods — zero set or complexity diffs between versions.
- Updated the stale tool pin in AGENTS.md (said `0.2.1`) and annotated the three CI activation sites.

### How to verify
```bash
dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.10.0"
dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
dart pub global run crap4dart analyze   # Max CRAP 12.00 — OK (threshold 12.00)
dart pub global run crap4dart check     # 2 gates passed, 0 warned
python3 scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down <base>   # badge/parity/only-down OK
```
Local CI-parity run (ambient `FA_*` stripped): 7898 tests passed; coverage 93.49% ≥ 80%; 0.9.5 and 0.10.0 report the identical max CRAP (12.0) on the same lcov.

### Notes for the next lane
- **Pre-existing, not from this change:** `test/cli/providers_queue_editor_test.dart` (3 tests: `move reorders and persists`, `remove 0 persists…`, `add appends…`) reads the REAL `Platform.environment` via `resolveProviderQueueAtBoot` (no `env:` seam) — running the suite from inside a fa session (which sets `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`) flips those edits onto the env-refusal arm and fails them. CI is unaffected; fixing needs a small env seam in `AgentCliConfig`.

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — the gate's per-file semantics and the
  # 0.10.0 `duplication.sources` cross-module key stay available if the
  # jscpd guards are ever retired
  duplication: {enabled: false}
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'
